messages:
Maria: Quick sync — we need a clear API for hybrid-precision negotiation. Proposal: let model owners publish a `quality_budget` (0-100) and have the runtime map requests into FP8/INT8/4-bit lanes based on workload and SLOs. Thoughts? @Lee @Oliver :thinking:
Lee: I like the simplicity. Two quick asks: (1) support per-customer overrides (enterprise wants control), (2) require a `safety_floor` that pins an absolute minimum quality metric so we never drop below X.
Oliver: Agree with both. We should tie `quality_budget` to measurable evals (per-model eval set) and surface a `deg_score` estimate at decision time. Runtime fallback should be explicit (e.g., auto-upgrade to fp16) when deg_score > threshold. Example profile snippet for discussion:
```
quant_profile: {
  quality_budget: 85,
  deg_threshold: 0.12,
  fallback: "fp16"
}
```
Syd: Ops note — we must expose expected p50/p95 latency impact per lane so customers can see cost/latency tradeoffs. Also make batching behavior predictable when lanes mix (don't let small fp16 fallbacks kill batching efficiency). Tag telemetry with `quant_lane` and `decision_reason`.
Ana: How about per-request hints vs server-side policy? My suggestion: allow optional header `X-Precision-Hint: aggressive|balanced|conservative` that runtime can honor if it doesn't violate the pinned `safety_floor` or tenant lock. For private deployments support `X-Precision-Lock: true` so infra teams can force exact behavior.
deploy-bot: canary deployed quant-negotiation v0.2 to staging :rocket: — tracing enabled, sampling=1%
Maria: Great feedback. Action items: I'll open an RFC PR that includes (a) profile schema with `quality_budget`+`safety_floor`, (b) runtime decision flow with `deg_score` checks, (c) telemetry contract, (d) header wire-format. Can someone volunteer to own the perf experiments to quantify p95 deltas across fp8/int8/4bit? @Syd?
Syd: I can take perf experiments. Will sketch a measurement plan tomorrow. :+1:
Maria: Thanks — will tag owners in the RFC. Keeping this thread as the follow-up for interface debate.
